note: The BASE half of the promulgation boundary: what the harness scaffold writes that belongs to no single artifact. Each activated governance package ships its own ownership.json fragment for its artifact's paths; sync composes base + fragments (Plan-033, ADR-0019). Read this file; never re-decide a path's class at the call site. The prose that explains the four classes is plugin/references/ownership.md.

classes.norm: This tooling owns it. Promulgation overwrites it, and a local edit is drift to be reconciled rather than a preference to be preserved.
classes.shaped: Two owners, permanently (Plan-031): the tooling owns the structure — migration may restructure it per a recorded note — and the repository owns every word of the content. Promulgation never writes here; this is migration's class.
classes.seed: Written once when absent, never overwritten. The repository owns it from the moment it exists.
classes.repo: Never written and never read for a decision. Promulgation that would touch one of these stops and reports.

paths.why: The record lifecycles, which this tooling defines. Measured 2026-08-13 as divergent in three of three repositories checked and divergent from the shipped copy — that divergence is unreconciled drift, not per-repository preference, and it is the reason this declaration is being written.
A mechanical import of AGENTS.md and nothing else. Byte-identical in every repository measured 2026-08-13.
Symlinks into .agents/rules/. Pure mechanism with no content of its own; a repository editing one has broken the bridge rather than expressed a preference.
The manual entrypoint to the gate. Wiring, not policy.
The runner that composes the fragments. A repository holding its own copy shadows the live one silently, which is the failure this class prevents.
Wiring with no check logic, resolving everything from the repository root. Measured 2026-08-13 as carrying no machine-specific path in any repository checked or in the shipped template.
Authored once against the repository it describes, then maintained by whoever works there. Overwriting it would discard the map it exists to be.
Measured 2026-08-13 as four distinct files across four repositories. The divergence is legitimate: it is the human-facing description of one repository's governance.

Ships with a placeholder the setup skill explicitly tells the operator to fill in or delete. Measured 2026-08-13 at 1.1K in one repository and 9.4K in another — the shipped file is a prompt, not content.
Presentation, owned by the repository from its first edit.
Formatting and exclusion preferences. Identical across repositories so far, which is not authority to overwrite the first one that diverges on purpose.
The build baseline. Scaffolded once; every dependency added afterwards belongs to the repository.
Continuous-integration wiring the repository adapts to its own jobs and runners.
A documentation skeleton whose whole purpose is to be filled in.
Placeholders that let an empty directory survive. Once the directory has content they are deleted, and re-creating them would be noise.
The repository's own declared configuration. Promulgation may create it and must never rewrite what a repository declared about itself.
Clone-local and version-control-ignored. It is where the applied-version map is written, so promulgation updates that one key through the module that owns it — never by rewriting the file.

Investigations a person wrote; no governance package serves the type, so its class stays here in the base half. The record directories that used to share this entry moved to each type's own fragment as `shaped` (Plan-031).
A repository's own gate fragments, numbered to compose alongside the built-ins. The runner is the norm's; the fragments are not.

The declared exception. It dispatches to a pipeline this tooling's norm does not own and embeds an absolute path for that reason, which is why it stays clone-local and out of version control while its neighbour does not.
The repository's code. Named explicitly so that the absence of a match is never read as permission.
